locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:488 — "and `error()`s on any non-zero return, so the gate is reachable on a CI runner with no shim"
ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl:31-37 — `if code == 1 && !isempty(frozen) && !haskey(ENV, "GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP") … println("makedocs: SKIPPED …"); return nothing end`
src/CLI/Gate.jl:70-78 — frozen_rounds docstring: "the docs wrapper prints a skip line and exits 0 … gbg release and the deep doctor set [GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP], which turns the skip back into the refusal"
src/DocLints.jl:19-25 — the makedocs docstring's own body: "Any non-zero return is an `error`… Returns … `nothing` when an open round of a docs instrument froze the build … the skip is exit 0"
findings.resolution_hint: Add the SKIP mechanism to D9's makedocs bullet: describe the frozen_rounds/GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP behaviour (skip-not-fail on a frozen docs round; forced back to a refusal by gbg release and --deep), and soften "error()s on any non-zero return" to state the exception explicitly.
findings.description: D9's bullet on GBGCodingTools.makedocs states unconditionally that the wrapper error()s on any non-zero return from gate("check-docs", "check-consistency"). The actual extension body checks `code == 1 && !isempty(frozen) && !haskey(ENV, "GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP")` and, when true, prints a SKIPPED message and returns nothing — exit 0 — instead of erroring; only gbg release and the deep doctor force GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP=1 to get the refusal back. This SKIP-on-frozen-round mechanism is a deliberate, load-bearing design decision (it has its own rationale in the code: a red docs run should mean 'broken', not 'a round is open') but is entirely absent from ARCHITECTURE.md — the authoritative design record — which instead makes the flatly false claim that any non-zero gate return is an unconditional error(). This is exactly the false-but-plausible, RULE.DOC.VERIFIED-violating claim the rubric singles out: a reader would believe an open check-docs/check-consistency round always fails a docs/make.jl build, when in fact it silently succeeds (skips) by default.
findings.title: ARCHITECTURE.md claims makedocs "error()s on any non-zero return"; code SKIPS (exit 0) on a frozen docs round

findings.description: `TestHarness.oracle_registry` requires every public value-returning operation to be CLASSIFIED into one of five oracle classes, and only bars `relational`-only coverage; it does not require an independent reference for every operation. locations: instruments/check-consistency/workflow/rubric-audit.js:80-90 — stage 1: `.then(r => ({ key, ids, reported: (r && r.findings) || [] }))`
instruments/check-consistency/workflow/rubric-audit.js:92-93 — stage 2: `(run) => { if (!run) return null ...`
instruments/check-consistency/workflow/rubric-audit.js:127 — `dead: hatKeys.filter(k => !results[hatKeys.indexOf(k)])`
findings.resolution_hint: In stage 1, return null (not a wrapped object) when the agent died, e.g. `.then(r => r ? { key, ids, reported: r.findings || [] } : null)`, and track dead keys explicitly before scoring.
findings.description: Stage 1 of the pipeline() call always resolves to a truthy object, even when agent() died and returned null — the .then() wraps it unconditionally. Stage 2's liveness check (if (!run) return null) can therefore never fire from a stage-1 death, and the final dead computation on line 127 can likewise never see it. A blind-run hat that crashes is indistinguishable from one that genuinely found nothing: every finding id assigned to it is scored MISSED, silently corrupting the rubric audit's tally with no DEAD signal anywhere — the opposite of the pattern lanes.js, panel.js, audit.js and hunt.js all follow.
findings.title: rubric-audit.js's Blind-run pipeline stage converts a dead agent into a truthy 'reported nothing' result, so a dead hat is never flagged dead

findings.resolution_hint: After building units in batches mode, assert the union of batch ranges equals 1..A.findings.length (e.g. sum of unit item counts equals A.findings.length) and throw if not.
findings.description: `if (!batches.length) throw new Error('mode=batches needs a non-empty batches array covering EVERY finding')` (line 103) states in its own error text that batches must cover every finding, but the code never checks that the ranges in A.batches actually partition 1..A.findings.length with no gap or overlap. A gap between batch ranges silently produces zero items for those findings, and nothing downstream (the got < u.items.length check on line 143, or the written/dead/empty/truncated bookkeeping) can detect a finding that fell into such a gap: it is never assigned to any unit, never graded, and never reported as dead, empty, or truncated.
findings.title: verify-act.js's mode=batches guard claims full coverage but only checks that the batches array is non-empty

At bug-hunt grading, Passes.jl:619 sets entry["state"] = uppercase(String(r.status)) from a re-run witness, and Witnesses.jl documents/implements FIVE possible statuses: :pass, :fail, :broken, :blocked and :refused (a witness that loads something outside package/Test/stdlib, or that includes another file, is refused before it runs). :refused is missing from the enum entirely. If a witness is edited between passes to trip that refusal, entry["state"] becomes the string "REFUSED" and validate(load_schema("tally"), tally) at Passes.jl:668 then fails, throwing RoundError and crashing gbg round grade for that round.
findings.title: tally.schema.json's per_id.state enum omits REFUSED, a real witness status, so grade can crash

locations: src/CLI/Config.jl:8-12 — module docstring: "the two readers of the config's path vocabulary (globs and `file#heading` anchors)"
src/CLI/Config.jl:112-119 — `resolve_anchor(root, anchor)`

src/CLI/Seed.jl:47-51 — `select`: "A class's `anchor` here is a third sense of the word ... nor a hat's full-strength flag, which is what `Preflight.resolve_hats` returns."

findings.resolution_hint: Add `anchor` to the GBGCodingTools module map's bound-terms list with a one-line note that the CLI, config and seed subsystems each reuse the word for an unrelated concept (or rename one of the three uses, e.g. `heading_ref`/`hat_strength`/`seed_marker`), and have `Config.resolve_anchor`'s own docstring carry the disambiguating sentence Preflight and Seed already carry, since it is the sense a cold reader meets first.
findings.description: A cold reader who does `?Config` (the sixth file the module includes, long before Preflight or Seed) meets `anchor` defined only as a `file#heading` Markdown-heading locator (`resolve_anchor`), with nothing to suggest the word means anything else. That reading is reinforced at `?Init.derive_config`, which uses the same sense (`references anchors found by heading`). Only much later — at `Seed.select`, itself two files before the file that actually defines it — does a docstring admit the word has a second, unrelated sense (a hat's full-strength flag) and even call itself "a third sense of the word": three genuinely distinct technical meanings of one English word (a Markdown-heading pointer; a boolean meaning "runs at full strength, not on the economy model"; a seed class's placement regex) share the identifier `anchor` across the source, and the source itself (in a `#` comment the REPL never surfaces) concedes "Two unrelated senses of `anchor` meet in this one check." No module docstring — not even `GBGCodingTools`'s own map, which does define `consumer`, `instrument`, `round`, `lane`, `hat`, `Workflow` and `gate` — ever names `anchor` as an overloaded term of art, so nothing in the map warns the reader before the first (Config) sense is met. RULE.DOC.TERMS_DEFINED requires a term of art be defined (or disambiguated) at its first use under a cold read; here the FIRST use is not merely undefined, it is silently one of three incompatible things the same word will later mean.
findings.title: `anchor` carries three unrelated technical senses, none flagged as overloaded at its first (or second) use
